title: Beyond Robust Algorithmic Recourse: Sharing the Burden of Validity through Model Multiplicity
abstract: arXiv:2611.32543v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Algorithmic recourse provides actionable recommendations that enable individuals to achieve favourable outcomes. Implementing recourse for individuals requires significant time and effort, thus emphasizing robust recourse: recommendations that remain valid even under future model updates. While robustness preserves validity, we show it introduces systematic harms by constraining feasible recommendations to regions that disproportionately reflect majority behavior, reducing individual flexibility and amplifying disparities. Thus, non-robust recourse risks invalidation, whereas robust recourse creates a preference for high-density regions in the data that induces unfairness. However, this trade-off is driven by an implicit assumption that individuals alone should bear the burden of validity. We challenge this narrative and show that strategic model selection can help maintain validity while relaxing robustness requirements for individuals.

translated_title: 超越鲁棒算法追索：通过模型多重性分担有效性负担
translated_abstract: 算法追索为个体提供可操作的建议，使其能够获得有利的结果。为个体实施追索需要大量的时间和精力，因此强调了鲁棒追索的重要性：即使在未来的模型更新下仍然有效的建议。虽然鲁棒性能够保持有效性，但我们证明它会引入系统性伤害，因为它将可行的建议限制在不成比例地反映多数人行为的区域，降低了个体灵活性并放大了差异。因此，非鲁棒追索面临失效风险，而鲁棒追索则倾向于数据中的高密度区域，从而引发不公平。然而，这种权衡是由一个隐含假设驱动的，即个体应当独自承担有效性的负担。我们挑战了这一观点，并证明策略性的模型选择可以在放宽个体鲁棒性要求的同时帮助维持有效性。
tldr: 该论文揭示了鲁棒算法追索虽能保证建议有效性但会因偏向数据高密度区域而造成系统性不公平，并提出利用模型多重性下的策略性模型选择来分担有效性负担，从而在放宽个体鲁棒性要求的同时维持追索的有效性。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that robust algorithmic recourse preserves validity but introduces systematic unfairness by favoring high-density data regions, and shows that strategic model selection under model multiplicity can share the burden of validity, maintaining recourse validity while relaxing robustness requirements for individuals.
